transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Everyone keeps saying I’m overreacting, but I know certain people in town are targeting me, and nothing anyone shows me changes what I know is true. My family basically forced me to come here because they think I'm crazy, but I know what is actually going on.
How long have you been feeling this way, and when did you first notice that people in town were targeting you?

This all really started a little over a year ago, right after I lost my sales job and had to move back in with my relatives. It has been happening consistently ever since then, and it hasn't let up at all.
Have you also experienced hearing voices or seeing things that other people cannot hear or see?

No, I’ve never heard voices or seen things that aren't actually there. My mind is completely clear, it's just that these people in town are actually coordinating against me and I can see the real-world proof of it.
Apart from these concerns about being targeted, have you had any trouble organizing your thoughts, or have you experienced a major loss of motivation to do your daily activities?

No, my thoughts are perfectly organized and I haven't lost any motivation at all. If people would just stop acting like I'm crazy, they'd see I can handle normal day-to-day things like helping around the house, running errands, and taking care of myself without any issues.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are not your own, such as someone putting thoughts into your mind or broadcasting them so others can hear?

No, absolutely not, my thoughts are completely my own and no one is putting ideas in my head or broadcasting them. I’m just observing the real things that people around town are actually doing. It's all based on real actions I see with my own eyes.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were F20 and F22. Based on the interview, the patient has experienced persistent persecutory beliefs for over a year without any hallucinations, thought insertion, thought broadcasting, disorganization, or negative symptoms. Their daily functioning and motivation remain well-preserved. This clinical picture of a systematized, isolated delusional system lasting more than three months in the absence of clear schizophrenic symptoms strongly points to F22 (Delusional disorder) and makes F20 highly unlikely.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent persecutory delusion of being targeted by people in town, which has been consistently present for over a year. The patient explicitly denies hallucinations, disorganized thoughts, negative symptoms, and passivity phenomena (such as thought insertion or broadcasting). Daily functioning outside of the delusional system is relatively preserved, which aligns with the criteria for a persistent delusional disorder rather than schizophrenia.
